Plate hole used by this build: a screw through the board into a standoff.
Plate hole for a printed part.
Plate hole this build doesn't use.
Corners go on all four corners of the plate.
The Center Support goes under the plate, with the Center Support Retainer on top, under Backplane 2. The
boards stand clear of the retainer on their standoffs.
Each Backplane position takes a Backplane or a Backplane Pro. They have the same size and the same holes, in
every revision. The Backplanes and the Backplane Helper are turned 180° from their PCB files, with their bus
connectors to the left and their card slots toward the front.
Keyboard Encoder Helper Rev 1.0, the board on sale, has 88 × 39 mm holes. To fit one, drill holes 9 and 21
out to 5 mm, and put their screws 1 mm to the left of center.
The plate is a stack of three 3 mm acrylic layers, each cut from Plate.svg. Plate.svg is drawn turned 180°
The SVG is drawn 1:1, so it can be printed at full size to check a plate.
A normal hole, from the bottom up: an M3 × 12 pan head through the back of the plate, a female-male
standoff, the board, a female-female standoff, the top, and an M3 × 6 pan head.
Corners: an M3 × 16 countersunk screw from the top, through the plate, into a nut in the Corner's lower
Center Support: an M3 × 16 countersunk screw from the top, through the retainer and the plate, into a
nut in the Center Support. Four of these.
Rubber feet: one in the Ø10 recess under each Corner and under the Center Support.
Looking down on the plate, as the computer is used. All dimensions in mm.
